claims.text: Large language models are systematically more confident when providing reasoning before answering multiple choice questions.
The increase in confidence from reasoning before answering is larger when the selected answer is incorrect than when it is correct.
Chain-of-Thought prompting degrades model calibration by increasing the proportion of high-confidence wrong answers.
In multiple choice question evaluation settings with Chain-of-Thought prompting, LLM-estimated probabilities should be used with caution.

evidence.description: Experiments on a general knowledge benchmark, covering 57 subjects and seven LLMs, show systematic confidence increase with reasoning.
Experimental evaluations across 57 subjects and seven LLMs demonstrated a larger confidence jump on incorrect responses.
Standard calibration metrics such as Expected Calibration Error and Brier score showed increased proportions of high-confidence wrong answers.

methodologies.name: Confidence and Calibration Evaluation under Direct vs CoT Answering
methodologies.description: Evaluated response confidence and model calibration across direct and Chain-of-Thought answering modes on a multi-subject benchmark.

limitations.text: Chain-of-Thought reasoning alters token probabilities based on self-generated text, leading to inflated confidence estimates and degraded calibration.
